From debt to financial stability: mangaluru based delivery partner finds hope on the road.

Jul 29, 2026

For some, delivering food is just a job. But for Melwyn D'Souza, becoming a delivery partner bailed him out of a financial crisis.

Melwyn once led a simple life and as the elder son, he proudly shouldered family responsibilities. Melwyn's mother was recovering from a stroke and required constant medical care, and he was also financially supporting his younger brother's education. While circumstances were difficult, Melwyn was living a content life, grateful that he could take care of his family and contribute financially. "I was a happy go lucky guy, braving every difficult situation. I never got bogged down." he recalls.

However, everything changed when a close friend's betrayal left him with a substantial debt. This was a huge financial setback for Melwyn and added to his already difficult circumstances. "I couldn't believe it. My friend ran away with the money and I was left stranded without financial support." Melwyn said. "But, I couldn't run away. I knew my family still depended on me. I knew I had to work harder to manage it all."

Over the next few years, Melwyn took on different jobs, working as a cashier at a college and even opening a fast-food restaurant. While these efforts kept him afloat, neither provided enough to cover the mounting expenses of medical care and education for his family, and the loan repayment, which had grown to almost Rs 20 lakh with interest.

Seeking a higher yet steady income, Melwyn joined Swiggy in 2018 and has been working with the platform ever since."I went to a Swiggy hiring drive with very low expectations, as I never imagined delivery work could pay so well. Looking back, it's hard to believe how far I have come. I have almost cleared my debt and also invested in two bikes." he shared.

Apart from the financial independence, the biggest blessing for Melwyn has been the ability to take care of his mother. "Though she is recovering well, she has trouble walking and needs to take medicines twice a day. Working with Swiggy gives me the flexibility to go home and take care of her during the day."

Feeling hopeful about the future, Melwyn shared that the past five years were spent repaying his loan, and he feels his life has just begun. He is excited about the future and looks forward to living a happy and peaceful life.

Swiggy replaces Amitesh Jha with former Myntra CEO Nandita Sinha at Instamart.

Swiggy has appointed former Myntra CEO Nandita Sinha to lead Instamart from August 3 after Amitesh Kumar Jha resigned. She will steer the quick commerce business's next phase of growth.

By Vivek Dubey July 28, 2026, 12:52:32 PM IST (Published)

Swiggy Ltd. on Tuesday appointed former Myntra CEO Nandita Sinha as the CEO of its quick commerce business, Instamart, with effect from August 3, 2026. She succeeds Amitesh Kumar Jha, who resigned with immediate effect on July 28 to pursue other opportunities.

Sinha will be designated as a Senior Management Personnel (SMP) from August 3, while Jha ceased to be an SMP from July 28, according to the company's regulatory filing.

Swiggy Managing Director and Group CEO Sriharsha Majety said, "I am delighted to welcome Nandita Sinha as the CEO of Instamart." He added that her customer focus and operational discipline would help lead the platform's next phase of growth.

According to the company statement, Jha resigned with immediate effect to pursue opportunities outside the company. Swiggy said it places on record its appreciation for his contribution and guidance during his association with the company.

During his tenure, he led Instamart through a key phase of expansion, strengthened the platform's differentiation with launches such as Noice and improved its contribution margins.

Sinha's background

Sinha joins Swiggy after serving as CEO of Myntra. She has more than two decades of experience across consumer internet, e-commerce and FMCG, with leadership roles at Myntra, Flipkart, Britannia and Hindustan Unilever.

An alumna of IIT (BHU) and FMS Delhi, she led Myntra to become India's largest fashion e-commerce business after achieving EBITDA profitability in 2024.

Sinha said, "I have long admired what the team at Instamart has built. It's a business with a strong customer-first culture, great talent and significant opportunities ahead."

She added that she looked forward to working with colleagues, partners and consumers to shape the platform's next chapter of growth.

Swiggy said Sinha will lead Instamart's next phase by building on its differentiated assortment strategy, growth momentum, improved profitability metrics, customer focus and operational excellence.

Launched in August 2020, Instamart currently operates in more than 131 cities across India.

Swiggy Instamart CEO Amitesh Jha resigns, Nandita Sinha to take charge.

Former Myntra chief executive Nandita Sinha will take over as CEO of Swiggy Instamart from August 3, following Amitesh Kumar Jha's resignation.

At Instamart, Sinha will lead the platform's next phase of growth, building on its assortment strategy, improving profitability metrics and strengthening customer focus and operational efficiency

Amitesh Kumar Jha, chief executive officer (CEO) of quick-commerce platform Swiggy Instamart, has tendered his resignation with immediate effect to pursue other opportunities, according to a stock exchange filing on Tuesday.

Former Myntra CEO Nandita Sinha will take charge of Instamart from August 3.

"Nandita Sinha shall be appointed as the CEO of Instamart and categorised as the SMP (senior managerial personnel)," the filing said.

In her previous role at Myntra, Sinha led the platform as it became one of the country's largest fashion e-commerce businesses and continued to gain market share in a highly competitive segment after achieving earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) profitability in 2024.

A consumer internet industry veteran with more than two decades of experience, Sinha has built and scaled businesses across fashion, e-commerce and fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG). She has held leadership roles at Flipkart, Britannia Industries and Hindustan Unilever.

At Instamart, Sinha will lead the platform's next phase of growth, building on its assortment strategy, improving profitability metrics and strengthening customer focus and operational efficiency.

The leadership change comes as Swiggy seeks Indian-owned and controlled company (IOCC) status, which would allow it to directly own and sell inventory. The move is expected to improve margins and give the company greater control over its supply chain.

The proposal will be discussed at Swiggy's annual general meeting (AGM) on August 18, about two weeks after Sinha takes charge.

Speaking about her new role, Sinha said: "I have long admired what the team at Instamart has built. It's a business with a strong customer-first culture, great talent and significant opportunities ahead. Instamart sits at the heart of how India shops for its everyday needs, and I look forward to working with our colleagues, partners and consumers to shape its next chapter of growth."

Commenting on Sinha's appointment, Sriharsha Majety, managing director and group CEO of Swiggy, said: "I am delighted to welcome Nandita Sinha as the CEO of Instamart. Nandita is one of India's most accomplished consumer internet leaders, and I'm enthusiastic about the vision, customer obsession and operational rigour she brings to the team we've built at Instamart."

Majety said Jha had provided valuable leadership to Instamart, guiding the platform through a period of growth, strengthening its differentiation through launches such as Noice and improving its contribution-margin trajectory.

"Over his tenure, he has been instrumental in scaling Instamart through a critical growth phase, building a strong, high-performing culture, and leaving the organisation in a solid, well-run state. We extend our best wishes to him for his future endeavours," Majety added.

Jha joined Instamart as CEO in September 2024 after spending more than a decade at Flipkart. He succeeded Phani Kishan, who had previously led the quick-commerce business.

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

Swiggy Instamart appoints Gautam Swaroop as chief business officer.

The development comes a week after Hari Kumar, who was the then CBO, resigned from the company.

Swaroop will oversee Instamart's commercial operations, including customer growth, category management, brand partnerships and business expansion

Quick commerce platform Swiggy Instamart on Wednesday appointed Gautam Swaroop as its chief business officer (CBO).

In his new role, Swaroop will oversee Instamart's commercial operations, including customer growth, category management, brand partnerships and business expansion.

The appointment comes a week after Hari Kumar, the company's former CBO, resigned. Around the same time, chief operating officer Ankit Jain also stepped down.

Swaroop brings more than two decades of experience across consulting, pharmaceuticals and technology.

He began his career at McKinsey & Company, where he spent a decade working on strategy and operations transformation. He later joined Dr. Reddy's Laboratories, where he helped scale the company's emerging markets business from $37 million to $190 million in revenue.

Most recently, Swaroop served as chief executive officer of the international business at hospitality technology firm Oyo, where he led operations across the United States, the United Kingdom, Europe, China and Latin America, taking the business to profitability.

"I'm excited to join Instamart at such an important juncture in its growth journey. I look forward to partnering with the teams across the business to drive growth, build stronger consumer and partner experiences, and create enduring value as we scale," Swaroop said.

Girish Menon, Swiggy's chief human resources officer, said Instamart is at an important stage as it expands its assortment across categories and consumption occasions while deepening partnerships with brands.

"Gautam brings deep expertise and a proven track record of scaling businesses in dynamic, fast-paced industries, and his leadership will be beneficial as we continue to deliver unparalleled convenience to consumers," Menon said.

Swaroop's appointment is part of a broader strengthening of Instamart's leadership team. The platform has also appointed Srikar Adavi as vice-president, Ad Monetization, and Hardeep Kaur as associate vice-president, Category (FMCG), among other senior hires.

Instamart currently operates in more than 131 cities through over 1,143 dark stores and has 13.3 million average monthly transacting users.

Swiggy Instamart elevates Dhanya Hemanth Raj to Director - Marketing.

In her new role, Raj will oversee marketing strategy, brand communication and brand-building initiatives for Swiggy Instamart, prior to which she served as General Manager Marketing.

12 Jun 2026 19:01 IST

Swiggy Instamart has promoted Dhanya Hemanth Raj to the role of Director - Marketing. She announced the appointment in a post on LinkedIn.

"Excited to share that I've been promoted to Director, Marketing at Swiggy Instamart!

It's been one hell of a journey, and I'm incredibly grateful to the leaders and teams who have backed me along the way," she wrote.

In her new role, Raj will oversee marketing strategy, brand communication and brand-building initiatives for Swiggy Instamart.

Before the promotion, she served as General Manager Marketing at Swiggy Instamart, where she led marketing budgets, media strategy and brand campaigns for the quick commerce platform and its private label business.

Prior to joining Swiggy Instamart, Raj was Head of Brand Marketing at TenderCuts, where she led brand awareness and growth initiatives for the meat delivery company.

Earlier, she worked as Brand Manager at Licious, contributing to national marketing campaigns and brand development efforts. She also held strategy and planning roles at advertising agencies including MullenLowe Lintas Group and R K Swamy BBDO, where she worked on brands across sectors such as retail, food delivery, financial services and automotive.

Raj's earlier career included consumer insights and market research roles at Converseon in the United States, as well as communications experience with Weber Shandwick and the Association for Computing Machinery.

Restaurant India news: Swiggy elevates Akhil Juluru and Ashwin Chand to Director roles.

Swiggy has elevated two senior executives, Akhil Juluru and Ashwin Chand, to Director-level positions as the company continues to strengthen its leadership structure across its food marketplace business.

The appointments were announced separately by the executives through LinkedIn posts and reflect Swiggy's continued focus on leadership development and internal talent progression as it expands its food delivery and commerce operations.

Akhil Juluru has been promoted to Director - Business within Swiggy's Food Marketplace division. Announcing the development, Juluru wrote, "New Chapter: Director - Business at Swiggy! I'm incredibly excited to share my promotion within the Food Marketplace business."

Prior to this elevation, Juluru served as General Manager - Business, where he was involved in driving business growth initiatives and marketplace strategy. In his new role, he is expected to oversee key business priorities and contribute to the continued expansion of Swiggy's food marketplace operations.

In a separate leadership move, Ashwin Chand has been promoted to Director of Business after serving as General Manager - Discounting Strategy. Chand has been associated with Swiggy for more than seven years, having joined the company in January 2019.

During his tenure, Chand played a significant role in shaping the company's discounting framework and broader business strategy initiatives. Before joining Swiggy, he worked with ride-hailing platform Ola, gaining experience in large-scale consumer technology operations.

The promotions come at a time when food delivery platforms are increasingly focusing on operational efficiency, customer retention, restaurant partnerships and sustainable growth. As competition intensifies across food delivery and quick commerce segments, leadership continuity and internal capability building have become key priorities for major players in the sector.

Swiggy remains one of the most influential marketplace platforms, connecting millions of consumers with restaurant partners across India. The elevation of Juluru and Chand signals the company's continued investment in experienced leadership as it navigates the next phase of growth across food delivery, quick commerce and related business verticals.
